_comment: Per-scene floors for tools/perceptual_gate.py, calibrated 2026-09-20 from
measurement, not invented. Two sources:
(a) the exact-reference build against itself in the two configurations
it already ships -- golden (--interp, --quantum 128, serial) against
default (--quantum 0, threads). Most scenes are byte-identical; the
spread comes from the interleave, and it is the floor of variation
a build we fully trust already produces.
(b) sm64 golden against --timing-oc, which is the closest thing in the
tree to the model Phase 1 installs: mean 0.9999, p01 0.9960,
min 0.9760 with the +/-2 alignment window.
Measured (a), all 1800 frames unless noted:
sm64 / dbori / mlbis / meteos / gsdd(300)  exact
artacd   mean 1.0000  p01 1.0000  min 0.9981  psnr min 40.9
etody    mean 1.0000  p01 0.9998  min 0.9772  psnr min 39.0  (223 realigned)
st-intro mean 0.9998  p01 0.9983  min 0.9970  psnr min 41.0  (600 frames)
The metric floors are deliberately looser than those numbers: they exist to
catch gradual degradation across a phase, while the structural faults --
which no floor excuses and which are checked separately -- catch the
failures that actually matter. Tighten a scene's row when a phase lands
and the measurement supports it; never loosen one without recording why.
